name: malformed
description:
Rows that must be skipped without ending the walk, and values that must not abort the script.

Both arrays carry a bare string where the schema documents an object; calling .get on a string aborts a Starlark run outright, so the type is checked before the record is read. Two device rows carry no usable uid -- one null, one empty -- and are dropped rather than given a synthesized id, because a random fallback creates a brand new asset on every poll. The skips are tallied and reported as one line rather than one line per record, which is what a large estate needs.

The surviving device is deliberately awkward: mac_list arrives as a bare string instead of an array, ip_list holds a null beside a real address and a link-local one that identifies nothing, first_seen_list holds an unparseable timestamp, and last_seen_list holds a timestamp in 2099. That last one is the dangerous value: an un-clamped future timestamp makes the platform drop the whole asset, which is why the script never parses a timestamp by hand. A relation row with a null device_uid and a cve_ids list holding a null and a non-CVE string must contribute nothing and fail nothing.

devices_vulnerabilities.vulnerability_name: Advisory with a partly unusable CVE list

log_contains: skipped 3 device records with no uid
